candidates.exact_span:
Procedures for Implementing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Permits in New
Mexico, March 2012.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If this reference is interpreted as incorporating New Mexico NPDES implementation procedures into the permit basis, it could change which numeric limits are treated as enforceable and which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable; if treated as non-operative background reading, neither limit nor monitoring computations would draw on it.

candidates.exact_span: Statewide Water Quality Management Plan, December 17, 2002.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this plan is an operative source of monitoring obligations (versus a historical planning document) could change which monitoring requirements are established as required, not required, or unresolved for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: State of New Mexico 303(d) List for Assessed Stream and River Reaches, 2018 -2020.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this cited 303(d) listing is treated as governing impairment status for the permitted reach—and whether the 2018–2020 cycle is the operative listing for FY2025—could change identification of applicable numeric limits and impairment-triggered monitoring duties; treating it as non-operative bibliography would exclude those effects.

candidates.exact_span:
EPA Region 6 "Policy for Post Third Round NPDES Permitting" and "Post Third Round NPDES
Permit Implementation Strategy," October 1, 1992.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If interpreted as binding implementation policy incorporated by reference, these documents could alter which permit limits and monitoring conditions are deemed applicable; if interpreted as superseded or informational only, limit and monitoring obligation computations would differ.

candidates.exact_span:
2014 Review Water Quality Standards for Salinity - Colorado River System, Colorado River
Basin Salinity Control Forum - October 2014.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this salinity standards review is an incorporated basis for enforceable salinity/TDS limits could change which numeric limits are selected for compliance comparison; treating it as background would exclude those limits from Purpose A evaluation.

candidates.exact_span:
Bureau of Reclamation. 2013. Quality of Water – Colorado River Basin Progress Report
No. 24. Upper Colorado Region, Salt Lake City, UT
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this report is read as establishing or supporting operative salinity/TDS discharge criteria versus non-binding technical background could change which numeric limits are deemed applicable for Colorado River-related parameters.

candidates.exact_span:
Navajo Nation Surface Water Quality Standards 2007, passed by Navajo Nation Resources
Committee on May 13, 2008 (Effective March 26, 2009)
candidates.computation_change_reason: If these standards are interpreted as the governing water quality criteria for the discharge reach, applicable numeric limits and any standards-dependent monitoring could differ from New Mexico-only criteria; if interpreted as inapplicable or merely contextual, Purpose A and B results would not incorporate them.

candidates.exact_span:
Pimentel, R. and R. V. Bulkley. 1983. Concentrations of total dissolved solids preferred or
avoided by endangered Colorado River fishes. Transactions of the American Fisheries Society
112:595-600.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this TDS/fisheries study is an operative basis for numeric TDS limits (e.g., species-protection-derived criteria) versus non-operative scientific background could change which enforceable TDS limits are identified and compared against reported measurements.
